For a few brief moments this week, those passing by the Kennedy Center in Washington could see for themselves that President Donald Trump’s name had, in fact, been removed.

That space has been covered by a tarp since June. But as footage obtained by NBC Washington shows, that tarp was loosened by a Thanksgiving storm, leaving the empty space temporarily visible.

The Kennedy Center’s board, which Trump has stacked with his own allies, had his name added to the building last year, turning it into “The Donald J. Trump and John F. Kennedy Memorial Center For The Performing Arts,” as seen in this image from June:

However, a judge later ordered the removal of Trump’s name.

“The Kennedy Center’s organic statute makes crystal clear that the Center is to be named for President Kennedy, and it cannot bear any other formal name or public memorial based on the Board’s unilateral say-so,” U.S. District Judge Christopher Cooper ruled in May. “Congress gave the Kennedy Center its name, and only Congress can change it.”

His name was yanked off the building in June ― but a tarp was erected to hide the work. The New York Times reported in September that Matt Floca, who Trump named executive director, had the tarp put in place because he worried footage of the removal would anger the president.

The tarp has remained in place ever since ― the center told the Times it was there for “maintenance” ― until this week’s storm briefly pulled part of it down.

By Friday, the tarp had been fixed, again covering up the space where Trump’s name had been:

Trump has, in fact, been angered by the removal of his name. He wrote on Truth Social in September that if the judge doesn’t allow his name on the building, then “the Reconstruction and the Renovation of The Kennedy Center will not take place.”

There is also concern he may attempt to demolish the facility entirely if he can’t name it for himself, and he was recently seen looking at images of the site with the word “DEMOLISH” visible.
